lens: POD-model faithfulness and the LW1 door (M1-M4 expressibility, may_cover vs TAMPURA's mesh, the fixed-eye question, CLAIM EFFECT wording for abstract.tex:18 / results.tex:295,300,352,354 / conclusion.tex:10,27-45, the unresolved-parking statement)

findings.title: Parked (unresolved) fragments ARE asserted known-not-here to the planner; P4.5 and P4.8 state the opposite
findings.plan_location: P4.5 CORRECTIONS (lines 525-527), P4.8 KEPT OPEN (lines 615-616), G5 (lines 90-93)
findings.problem: The plan says the 3-strike give-up 'parks a fragment unresolved and never asserts it empty' and lists 'no region ever asserted empty without an observation (unresolved parking stays the only bound)' as an LW1 invariant kept open. That is true only of the BeliefState bookkeeping. The loop passes parked fragments to the planner inside known_empty (test_full_pipeline.py:1217-1218: known_empty = get_known_empty_shadows() + get_parked_shadows()), and _build_init emits (obj_at_boxel_KIF target frag) for every known_empty fragment (pddlstream_planner.py:638-640). In the Know-If encoding, KIF without obj_at_boxel means 'known, and not here' (methods.tex:135), so in the planner's symbolic belief a parked region is indistinguishable from an observed-empty one: K(not InBoxel) is asserted without an observation. G5 itself accepts mark_unresolved as valid provenance for a known_empty id, so the plan's own gate encodes the thing P4.8 says never happens. The honesty lives only in the exit reason (blocked_giveup_shadows, test_full_pipeline.py:1048-1056) and in BeliefState.
findings.evidence: test_full_pipeline.py:1217-1218; pddlstream_planner.py:638-640; belief.py:82-98; execution.py:3061-3079; plan lines 90-93, 525-527, 615-616
findings.required_change: Reword P4.5 and P4.8: 'a parked fragment is withheld from the planner by emitting the same Know-If literal as an observed-empty fragment; in the planner's belief it is indistinguishable from not_here; the distinction is kept in BeliefState and in the exit reason, and an episode that ends with parked fragments and no target is a failure (all_searched), while one that finds the target elsewhere is a success.' The paper prose must say this instead of either the thesis wording ('marked as not containing the target') or 'never asserts it empty'. G5's ledger must tag parked ids separately from not_here ids so the per-episode report can count them. Record the LW1-clean alternative (withhold is_shadow or boxel_fits for a parked fragment instead of emitting KIF, so it is unsensable rather than known) as a flagged BF# candidate that needs a main-pipeline A/B on our scenes; it is not to be done silently inside the bridge.

findings.title: D3's grasp_body = 'the contacted body's id (never the target's name)' can never satisfy TAMPURA's reward
findings.problem: TAMPURA's reward is Exists ?o over the 'physical' type: is-target(?o) and holding(?o) (env.py:993-1004). abstract() emits holding(grasp_body) with grasp_body whatever the observation carried (env.py:309-311) and is-target over the object SYMBOLS in world.objects (env.py:313-315). Their own pick writes grasp_body = the object symbol (env.py:394 obs.grasp_body = obj; env.py:350 action.args[0]). If our ObservationAdapter writes the pybullet body id, holding(<int>) never unifies with is-target(<symbol>) and every one of our episodes scores 0 regardless of what the arm did. The comparison would be invalid in the direction that looks most honest.
findings.required_change: D3: grasp_body = the store symbol whose body equals the contacted body (store.get(sym) == contacted_id, the same identity lookup their obs_from_camera_image uses at env.py:70-73), resolved from physical contact readback, never selected by name. Reword 'never the target's name' to 'never chosen by name; resolved from the contacted body through their store, and logged'. Add a positive control to the G6 unit tests: with both finger pads in contact with the die body and zero constraints, assert that their get_reward on the updated belief returns 1.0 when conf == DEFAULT_ARM_POS; today G6 only has negative controls, so the all-zero failure mode would pass every gate.

findings.title: The plan is inconsistent about whether the eye is the physical wrist camera at home or a fixed camera posed like it; the main loop renders from ~12 non-sense sites with the arm away from home
findings.problem: D4 says the fixed camera IS their wrist camera at DEFAULT_ARM_POS, 'no external camera is added', and 'a sense is only valid with the arm at the sensing configuration', which is the physical justification for M1. B2 instead builds 'camera params from the camera_frame link state at q_home' once and has detect_objects render from them on the executing client: that is a disembodied camera posed where the wrist camera would be at home, which keeps rendering while the arm is elsewhere. The main pipeline takes renders outside sense at execution.py:343 (census), 720/723 and 821 (integrity), 998, 1799, 1954, 2102 (retire_lost_objects) and test_full_pipeline.py:1936 (post-place carve, arm at the place pose), 2169. Under the virtual reading those observations come from a camera that is not on the robot (so D4's 'no external camera' is false in spirit and M1's at_config precondition is a modelling fiction that costs moves for no physical reason). Under the physical reading they come from the wrist camera at unplanned poses, i.e. a moving camera outside the planner's control, which contradicts the thesis's fixed-camera observation model (methods.tex:166, 170, 213) and G15. Either way the observation function O is not what the plan says it is.
findings.required_change: Decide once in D4 and record it as a BF# with BEFORE/AFTER. Option A (recommended; it is the thesis model unchanged): declare a fixed camera at the pose their wrist camera has at DEFAULT_ARM_POS, detached from the arm; drop M1's sense precondition (sense still calls no streams; methods.tex:170 stays literally true); keep M3; disclose that the viewpoint equals their generator's hidden-check viewpoint and that our own arm can occlude it (still_blocked handles that). Option B (physical wrist camera): keep M1 and add a gate G20: every render recorded in the ledger carries a joint readback within tolerance of q_home, and every non-sense render site is deferred until the arm is home or disabled for the bridge, which is a main-pipeline change needing its own A/B. The plan may not keep D4's physical wording with B2's virtual implementation.

findings.title: No CLAIM EFFECT line names the headline sentences abstract.tex:18, results.tex:295/300/354, conclusion.tex:10
findings.plan_location: P4.5 M1-M4 CLAIM EFFECT lines (lines 491-523), P4.6 RESULT TABLE / DISCLOSURES (lines 563-571)
findings.problem: The sentences the bridge exists to replace are not listed. abstract.tex:18 says 'on the closest analogous hidden-object task ... comparable end-to-end cost (about 144 s vs 166 s) and comparable reliability (65.6 % vs the >= 63 % implied)'; results.tex:295 adds 'on a marginally easier goal' and 'the two run on different environments, so it benchmarks neither system'; results.tex:300 repeats the numbers in the figure caption; results.tex:354 adds 'simpler to model than TAMPURA's learned probabilistic policy'; conclusion.tex:10 restates 'comparable end-to-end cost and reliability'. After a seed-for-seed run on their task, 'closest analogous', 'different environments', 'marginally easier' and 'implied by its reported returns' all become false, and 'comparable' is not pre-registrable: the campaign may show ours worse. 'Simpler to model' is also no longer free: we had to declare hollow classes, die and cup class sizes and (under M1) a sensing configuration, against their category meshes, grasp library and look confs. M4's CLAIM EFFECT is only 'the paper states both', and M2's says results.tex:352 'becomes stronger', which is spin: the interior region's existence is class knowledge, only its view-blocking is camera-derived.
findings.required_change: Add M5 HEADLINE SENTENCES with BEFORE (the quoted sentences) and AFTER as a template with blanks to be filled only from campaign.json ('On TAMPURA's Find Die, seed for seed over its 20 released episodes and three layouts, ours reached the goal in X/20 against Y/20 for TAMPURA, at t1 = ... vs ...'), and the CLAIM EFFECT rule: the parity adjectives are deleted now and are not reinstated unless the Wilson intervals support them; a worse result is written as such; the architectural paragraphs results.tex:315-352 stay. Change M2's CLAIM EFFECT to 'results.tex:352 unchanged, with the qualification that in find_dice the hidden region under a hollow object exists because of a declared class property, not because the camera cast it; its view-blocking and clearance are camera-derived as for lateral shadows'. Add a disclosure line listing the task knowledge each system was given (ours: hollow classes, class sizes, target class, sensing pose if M1; theirs: category meshes, saved grasp library, look confs, target class).

findings.title: 'may_cover' names a task role, and the parity sentence with TAMPURA's mesh overstates; recast M2 as a geometric class property that relaxes the thesis's solidity assumption
findings.problem: A declaration named may_cover whose members are exactly the cup classes of the find_dice task reads as 'cups hide dice' to a reviewer, even though the code is seed-generic. The plan's parity claim ('the same information TAMPURA takes from the known mesh') is stronger than the source supports: TAMPURA clears voxels within GRID_RESOLUTION/2 of EVERY known body's concave collision mesh, uniformly for all categories (env.py:222-237; use_concave=True at env.py:691), so hollowness is derived from geometry; ours is a hand-written per-category list that happens to coincide with the hiding classes. The thesis's own place where containment was excluded is the solidity assumption: the shadow caster subtracts the occluder footprint from its shadow (shadow_calculator.py:217-236) and the planner emits KIF for the target on every OBJECT boxel ('whole table observed', pddlstream_planner.py:683-694). The plan does not say so, and does not say that the interior region overlaps the cup's OBJECT boxel although the thesis calls the Boxels a partition (methods.tex:84, 97).
findings.required_change: Rename the property to a geometric one (hollow / has_cavity) declared per category with cavity dimensions measured once in B1 from the YCB mesh (inner footprint = AABB minus wall thickness, cavity height), and cast the interior region from those measured dimensions rather than the bare footprint to est_top, so the declaration carries the same geometric content TAMPURA reads from the mesh and generalises to any hollow class (3D Wumpus: any volume behind a cover). Write M2's POD JUSTIFICATION in the thesis's terms: the OBJECT boxel of a solid object is fully occupied (audit #67), so its footprint is removed from hidden space; for a declared hollow class that assumption is relaxed and the cavity rejoins the hidden space as its own region, cast by the object, cleared only by relocating it and observing the grid. State explicitly that the interior region overlaps the caster's OBJECT boxel and that the at-most-one-SHADOW-per-point invariant (audit #68) still holds. Rewrite the parity sentence: 'TAMPURA derives hollowness from the category's concave mesh for every object; we declare it per class because our perception yields boxes, not meshes; both take the category label from the scene.'

findings.title: If M1 is kept: the home pseudo-boxel and the identity of q_home with the planner's start config are unstated
findings.problem: M1 injects (Boxel home) and (config_for_boxel q_home home) so move can target q_home, mirroring the tray trick (pddlstream_planner.py:794-805). The 'home' object is a Boxel with neither is_shadow nor is_free_space nor is_object; any init loop that enumerates Boxel objects (placement candidates, boxel_fits, corridor facts) must skip it, and the plan does not say so. Also plan() defaults current_config to self.home_config (pddlstream_planner.py:246-247); if the task spec's q_home is a different symbol with identical joints, the first plan needs a zero-length move before the first sense, or sense is ungroundable at t=0.
findings.required_change: State in M1 that q_home IS the planner's home_config symbol (one object, two roles) and that the home pseudo-boxel is excluded from every init enumeration by a type check, with G10's domain diff and a B4 assertion on the generated init (no is_free_space/is_shadow/boxel_fits fact names 'home'). If Option A of the eye decision is taken, delete M1 and this item lapses.

findings.title: Frame coverage of the home-pose eye is not in B1: out-of-frame grid endpoints count as blocked and funnel into the parking path
findings.problem: The sense classifier counts an endpoint outside the image as blocked, never clear (perception.py:247-249; execution.py:195-201), which is the right LW1 behaviour but means a cavity or shadow near the edge of the home wrist camera's frame (640x480, fx=fy=525, about 63 by 49 degrees over a 0.4 by 0.8 m placement region) returns still_blocked three times and is parked, i.e. asserted known-not-here to the planner (finding 1). B1(e) only asserts that the die is absent from the three home masks; it does not record which task bodies and which cup footprints lie fully inside the frame, nor the table-plane footprint of the frustum. Without that number the campaign cannot tell an honest search failure from a sensor that could never see the region, and the per-layout stratification in P4.6 cannot be interpreted.
findings.required_change: Add to B1(e): the table-plane frustum footprint at DEFAULT_ARM_POS and, per scene file, the list of task bodies in the home segmentation and the fraction of each cup footprint inside the frame; record it in BF#2 and in the campaign disclosures. No scene is filtered; a cavity outside the frame is an honest failure for ours and an unknown body for theirs (their perception also sees only seg-mask bodies at home, env.py:64-73), which the paper states as symmetric.

findings.title: P4.8's LW1 shape of sense omits two live preconditions
findings.problem: P4.8 writes the observable as Y_R with Pre(Y_R) = view_clear(R) (plus at_config under M1). The live sense also requires (handempty) and (boxel_fits ?o ?region) (domain_pddlstream.pddl:174, 183). handempty is part of Pre(Y) (self-occlusion, domain:158-168); boxel_fits is a static applicability fact whose meaning depends on --sense-gate (off for the campaign, P4.8 OUT). An LW1 compilation of the groundings would need both listed; leaving them out makes the 'unchanged' claim in line 617-618 inaccurate.
findings.required_change: Write Pre(Y_R) = view_clear(R) and handempty (and at_config(q_sense) only if M1 survives the eye decision), with boxel_fits(o, R) as a static applicability literal, and note that under --sense-gate off it is emitted for every pair.

what_the_plan_gets_right: D2: one runtime schema through their own extension point, their rollout, Belief.update and get_reward untouched; no-op steps deep-copy the belief (policy.py:125-127), so a reward of 1.0 reached at step 0 persists to rewards[-1] without any bridge write.

D5 / M2 mechanism: the interior region enters as a SHADOW-typed region with blocks_view_at(cup, cup, region), so view_clear, the handempty gate, the corridor facts and the sense classifier all apply with zero PDDL edits; rejecting lift-and-look and a new region predicate is correct.
M3 as a goal form rather than a new go_home action keeps the move/plan-motion path the planner already owns; verifying at_config against joint readback is the right success check.

The observation side already behaves conservatively where it matters for LW1: out-of-frame endpoints count as blocked, not clear (execution.py:195-201), and every not_here write in the sense path is backed by a render of that fragment's grid (execution.py:2112-2118, 2222-2236, 2769).
The thesis-text corrections in P4.5 (0.10 m lift, SymK as an FD fork, derived predicates vs LW1 knowledge axioms) are accurate and needed.

Pre-registration discipline: budgets, repetitions, no re-runs of failed seeds, success computed only through their RolloutHistory (G12), constants derived once from declared class sizes (D7/G9), explicit disclosure list in P4.6.
D1 chooses the whole pipeline inside their world rather than a planner-only port, which is the only variant that tests the thesis claims rather than the planner alone.
